title: Stochastic convex bandits: two evaluations of the same sample and loss at the center.
summary: Each round generates a fresh random convex loss. The algorithm chooses two probe points in advance and receives both values from the same sample. Only the center incurs population mean loss. Sample Lipschitz constants are controlled in second moment and need not be uniformly bounded sample by sample.

model.instance: Samples $\xi_t$ are i.i.d. Each sample function $F(\cdot;\xi)$ is almost surely convex on $\mathbb R^d$, with a global random Lipschitz constant $G(\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E G(\xi)^2\le L^2$. The population function $f(x)=\mathbb E F(x;\xi)$ is finite. Centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$; both probes may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$.

unresolved_applicability: The following are different native protocols: two values with independent additive noise, probes that also incur loss, probes restricted to the domain, and an adaptive second probe within the same round.
description_paragraphs: Each round draws a fresh full random function $F(\cdot;\xi)$. Every sample function is convex and globally $G(\xi)$-Lipschitz. Only $\mathbb{E}[G(\xi)^2]\le L^2$ is required; individual samples need not satisfy $G(\xi)\le L$.
The population objective is $f$, with finite f = E F. Its optimizer is defined within the ball.
The center $x_t$ incurs the loss and is selected before seeing sample $\xi_t$. Its function value is not returned as a third response.
Both probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$ may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$. They must be chosen jointly before either response for the round is observed.
Require $d,T\ge1$ and $L,R>0$.
Action centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$, while the two probes have query domain $\mathbb{R}^d$; each has its own explicit feasibility conditions.

description_paragraphs: Two evaluations of the same sample:

$$
x_t\in B_2^d(R),\quad z_t^+,z_t^-\in\mathbb{R}^d\ \longmapsto\ \big(F(z_t^+;\xi_t),F(z_t^-;\xi_t)\big)
$$
Choose the center and both probes before drawing one fresh independent sample $\xi_t$.
Both values come from the same sample function indexed by $\xi_t$. There is no additional independent measurement noise.
Probes incur no additional loss. The center does not receive a free third value observation.
Queries within a pair are nonadaptive: the second point cannot depend on the first response.
Public inputs are $d,T,L,R$ and the root-mean-square sample Lipschitz bound. The sample distribution and realizations are hidden.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{(F,P)}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\xi_{1:T}}[R_T]$.

Take the supremum over fixed sample-function families F and distributions P.
Define the population f = E_ξ F first. Compare every f(x_t) with the same fixed population optimizer.
Finally take expectation over learner randomness and online samples ξ₁:T. Do not interchange the minimum and sample expectation.

bounds.derivation: Conditional on the current sample $\xi_t$, the two-point variance lemma gives $\mathbb E_u\|g_t\|_2^2\le cdG(\xi_t)^2$, where $G(\xi_t)$ is the sample function's Lipschitz constant. Averaging over the sample yields $cdL^2$; the bias uses $\mathbb EG\le L$. The common-sample difference cancels additive function offsets, so no function-level bound is needed. Choose smoothing radius $\delta_{\mathrm{sm}}$ small enough that $L\delta_{\mathrm{sm}} T\le LR\sqrt{dT}$ and apply online gradient analysis.

bounds.derivation: For any online learner, let $\bar x=T^{-1}\sum_tx_t$. Convexity of the ball makes the average feasible, and convexity of the function gives $\mathbb E[f(\bar x)-f^\star]\le\mathbb E R_T/T$. The source proves optimization error at least $(LR/24)\min\{1,\sqrt{d/T}\}$ for an interface allowing two evaluations per sample. The same transcript and averaged output respect that interface, giving the cumulative pseudo-regret lower bound when $T\ge d$.
